title: Use an adjacency matrix when many parts link to many others.
rule: Draw one row for each part a link starts from and one column for each part it reaches, in the same order, and shade each cell by its count on a sequential scale, with the count printed in it; leave an empty cell as the page inside a thin grid line. Group the parts with a gap between groups, number the columns and name the rows; on a phone, number the rows too and list the names under the grid. Give a class of links that differs in kind, such as lines of authority with no sign, an outline and a key entry of its own, never a step of the scale.
use_when: The reader asks which parts of a system connect to which, and the links are too many for lines to stay readable.

use_instead.when: A few senders and the amounts they sent
Links among items in a set order
Values across two categories, with no links

text: A grid never tangles, however many links it holds, and its rows and columns let a reader find any pair. It gives up the paths a network shows, so it suits counts between groups more than one route.
why.basis: Design judgment, from the chart system our founder and editor approved in November 2026

builders: Form adjacency-matrix: node work/build/chart-kit/oa-chart.mjs build s74; encode from, to, value and special (the count in the class with no sign); labels.order sets the parts, labels.groups the gaps, labels.steps the scale with its fills (seq-1 takes the context edge), labels.special_label the outlined class.
